copy.bis: Gisala sa barnacle ang gagmayng butang sa tubig-dagat, mao nga makatabang kini sa paghupot niini nga limpyo ug balanse.

copy.en:
Why do barnacles crowd together on rocks?

Being packed together keeps them safer and helps them find a partner to make babies.
copy.tl:
Bakit nagkakadikit-dikit ang mga barnacle sa bato?

Mas ligtas sila kapag magkakasama at mas madali silang makakahanap ng kapareha para magkaanak.
copy.bis:
Nganong nagtapok-tapok ang mga barnacle sa bato?

Mas luwas sila kung magkadaghan ug mas sayon nila makit-an ang kapikas aron managhan.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter

copy.en:
Do people ever eat barnacles?

Yes! The goose barnacle is eaten as a tasty, even pricey, seafood in some countries — not every barnacle is just a boat-clinger!
copy.tl:
May kinakaing barnacle ba?

Oo! Ang goose barnacle ay kinakain bilang masarap, minsan mahal pa, na pagkaing-dagat sa ibang bansa — hindi lahat ng barnacle ay pang-barko lang!
copy.bis:
Naay ginakaon nga barnacle?

Oo! Ang goose barnacle ginakaon isip lami, usahay mahal pa, nga seafood sa ubang nasod — dili tanan barnacle para lang sa barko!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: cloth woven from fibers like cotton or piña
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: The competency asks for useful things made from non-living materials and the natural materials used. The card describes a dress made from cotton or piña, which are plant fibers (living materials), not non-living materials. It shares the theme of useful items and natural materials but does not address non-living materials, so it is only related.

copy.en:
What is the baro't saya made of?

It’s a dress made of cloth woven from fibers like cotton or piña! The threads are interlaced together before being sewn.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ginagawa sa baro't saya?

Ito ay damit na gawa sa telang hinabi mula sa hibla gaya ng bulak o piña! Pinagsalit-salit ang sinulid bago tahiin.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gihimo sa baro't saya?

Kini usa ka sapot nga hinimo sa panapton nga gihabol gikan sa lanot sama sa gapas o piña! Mga hilo nga gisalapid una tahion.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions air pressure and the barometer, but it does not teach that air pressure is a basic characteristic used to describe weather. It focuses on the invention of the barometer, not on identifying weather characteristics. This is background knowledge about a weather instrument, not direct instruction for the competency.

copy.en: A scientist named Evangelista Torricelli invented the barometer way back in 1643 to measure air pressure!
copy.tl: Isang scientist na nagngangalang Evangelista Torricelli ang nag-imbento ng barometer noong 1643 para sukatin ang air pressure!
copy.bis: Usa ka scientist nga ginganlag Evangelista Torricelli ang nag-imbento sa barometer niadtong 1643 aron sukdon ang air pressure!

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a cooling/contraction structure (columnar joints) in basalt, not the identification or description of materials formed during volcanic eruptions (e.g., ash, tuff, lava types). It is only tangentially related to volcanic products.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions basalt and a rock feature but does not guide observation/collection of rocks or describe similarities/differences in texture, color, or grain crystal size. It does not support the exploration/classification skill of the competency.

copy.en:
How do hexagonal rock columns form?

When thick basalt lava cools slowly, it contracts into hexagonal columns called columnar joints, seen in some Philippine sea cliffs!
copy.tl:
Paano nabubuo ang mga hexagonal na hanay ng bato?

Kapag mabagal lumamig ang makapal na basalt lava, nagko-contract ito sa hexagonal columns na tinatawag na columnar joints!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagporma sa hexagonal nga mga haligi sa bato?

Kung hinay malamig ang makapal nga basalt lava, nagcontrakt kini sa hexagonal columns nga gitawag columnar joints!

copy.en: Bases often taste bitter and feel slippery when you touch them. You can feel this slippery texture every time you use soap!
copy.tl: Ang mga base ay kadalasang mapait at madulas kapag hinawakan. Nararamdaman mo ang pagiging madulas na ito tuwing gumagamit ka ng sabon!
copy.bis: Ang mga base sagad mapait ug madanlog kon hikapon. Gibati nimo kini nga madanlog nga texture matag higayon nga mogamit ka og sabon!

copy.en: All living things depend on the environment to supply their basic needs, which are food, water, and shelter.
copy.tl: Lahat ng living things ay umaasa sa environment para makuha ang kanilang mga pangunahing pangangailangan, na ang pagkain, tubig, at tirahan.
copy.bis: Ang tanang living things nagsalig sa environment aron makuha ang ilang mga batakang panginahanglan, nga mao ang pagkaon, tubig, ug kapuy-an.

copy.en: Some bats actually migrate to other places, just so they can follow the fruits and flowers they love to eat.
copy.tl: May mga paniki na lumilipat sa ibang lugar para lang sundan ang mga bunga at bulaklak na kinakain nila.
copy.bis: Adunay mga kabog nga mobalhin sa laing dapit aron sundon ang mga bunga ug bulak nga ilang gikaon.

copy.en: Many bats send sound from their mouth or nose, then catch the returning echoes with their large ears!
copy.tl: Maraming paniki ang naglalabas ng tunog sa bibig o ilong, at sinasalo ang bumabalik na alingawngaw gamit ang malalaki nilang tainga!
copy.bis: Daghang kabog ang mopagawas og tingog gikan sa baba o ilong, ug mosalo sa nagabalik nga alingawngaw pinaagi sa ilang dagkong dalunggan!

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about intrusive igneous rock bodies (batholiths) and erosion exposing mountain cores. It does not explain what volcanoes are or how they are formed, and it is not directly related to volcanic processes.

copy.en: A batholith is a huge body of intrusive igneous rock, usually granite, that formed deep underground. When erosion removes the rock above, it becomes a mountain range's core!
copy.tl: Ang batholith ay napakalaking intrusive igneous rock, karaniwang granite, na nabuo sa malalim na ilalim ng lupa. Kapag tinanggal ng erosion ang bato sa ibabaw, ito ang nagiging core ng bulubundukin!
copy.bis: Ang batholith dako kaayo nga intrusive igneous rock, kasagaran granite, nga naporma sa lawom ilalom sa yuta. Kon tangtangon sa erosion ang bato sa ibabaw, kini mahimong core sa bukid!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that bats use echolocation to find food, which is an example of an adaptation, but it does not describe how bats have changed to better suit their environment, nor does it use secondary sources. It only presents a current behavior without framing it as an evolutionary change.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many insect-eating bats use sound and its echo, called echolocation, to find food in the dark.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community

copy.en:
How do bats find food in the dark?

Many insect-eating bats use sound and its echo, called echolocation, to find food in the dark.
copy.tl:
Paano nakakahanap ng pagkain ang paniki sa dilim?

Maraming insect bat ang gumagamit ng tunog at alingawngaw nito, tinatawag na echolocation, para mahanap ang pagkain sa dilim.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpangita og pagkaon sa kabog sa kangitngit?

Daghang insect bat naggamit og tingog ug sa alingawngaw niini, gitawag og echolocation, aron makit-an ang pagkaon sa kangitngit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a bat's legs are too weak to run and take off from the ground
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions legs and their role in movement, but it does not describe outer body parts generally or their role in gathering food. It focuses on why bats hang upside down, not on observing/describing body parts as the competency requires.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: So it hangs upside down and simply lets go, dropping into the air to fly.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a behavioral adaptation (hanging upside down) but does not describe how animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage. It does not address evolutionary change or adaptation from secondary sources.

copy.en:
Why do bats hang upside down to take off?

Unlike birds, a bat's legs are too weak to run and take off from the ground. So it hangs upside down and simply lets go, dropping into the air to fly.
copy.tl:
Bakit nakabitin nang baligtad ang paniki bago lumipad?

Hindi tulad ng ibon, mahina ang paa ng paniki para tumakbo at lumipad mula sa lupa. Kaya nakabitin ito nang baligtad — bumibitaw lang ito at bumabagsak sa ere para lumipad.
copy.bis:
Nganong nagbitay og balitad ang kabog una molupad?

Dili sama sa langgam, huyang ang tiil sa kabog aron modagan ug molupad gikan sa yuta. Mao nga nagbitay kini og balitad — mobuhi ra kini ug mahulog sa hangin aron molupad.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: big fruit-eating bats called flying foxes hang together in tall trees during the day in groups called colonies, and they help nature by spreading fruit seeds around.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes bat roosting behavior and seed dispersal, but does not explain how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs. It lacks the dependency explanation required by the competency.

copy.en: In the Philippines, big fruit-eating bats called flying foxes hang together in tall trees during the day in groups called colonies, and they help nature by spreading fruit seeds around.
copy.tl: Sa Pilipinas, ang malalaking paniki na kumakain ng prutas, tinatawag na flying fox, ay nagsasama-samang nakabitin sa matataas na puno kung araw; tinatawag itong kolonya, at tumutulong sila sa kalikasan sa pagkalat ng buto ng prutas.
copy.bis: Sa Pilipinas, ang dagkong paniki nga mokaon og prutas, gitawag og flying fox, magdungan nga magbitay sa habog nga mga kahoy kon adlaw; gitawag kini og kolonya, ug motabang sila sa kinaiyahan sa pagkatag sa liso sa prutas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: cleaning its fur with its tongue and claws to keep its wings ready to fly at night
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions wings as an outer body part, but the role described is grooming, not moving or gathering food as required by the competency.

copy.en:
What does a bat do while hanging?

A bat grooms itself with its free wings — cleaning its fur with its tongue and claws to keep its wings ready to fly at night!
copy.tl:
Ano ang ginagawa ng paniki habang nakabitin?

Nag-aayos ang paniki gamit ang malayang pakpak nito — nililinis ang balahibo gamit ang dila at kuko para handa itong lumipad pagsapit ng gabi!
copy.bis:
Unsay buhaton sa paniki samtang nagbitay?

Nagaayo ang paniki sa iyang kaugalingon gamit ang gawasnong pako — ginlimpyohan ang balhibo pinaagi sa dila ug kuko aron andam molupad kon gabii na!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: All bats can see just fine
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses bat vision and behavior, not outer body parts (head, legs, wings) or their roles in movement and food gathering. No direct instructional support for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: All bats can see just fine
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about bats' vision, not the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It does not teach any of these characteristics directly.

copy.en:
Are bats really blind?

Nope! All bats can see just fine — they just love flying around in the dark.
copy.tl:
Totoo bang bulag ang mga paniki?

Hindi pala! Lahat ng paniki ay talagang nakakakita — mahilig lang sila gumala sa dilim.
copy.bis:
Tinuod ba nga buta ang mga kabog?

Dili diay! Ang tanang kabog makakita gyud — ganahan lang sila molihok sa kangitngit.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: Wing structure is not identifying head, legs or wings and their role to move and gather food.

assignedReviews.reason: Finger bones in a bat wing are not the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

copy.en:
What makes up a bat's wing?

A bat's wing is thin skin stretched over its long finger bones, almost like a webbed hand.
copy.tl:
Ano ang bumubuo sa pakpak ng paniki?

Ang pakpak ng paniki ay manipis na balat na nakaunat sa mahahaba nitong buto ng daliri, parang kamay.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang naghimo sa pako sa kabog?

Ang pako sa kabog kay nipis nga panit nga gibukhad sa iyang taas nga bukog sa tudlo, sama sa kamot.

assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that strong acids are dangerous; it does not teach identifying solutions as acids, bases, or salts using litmus indicator, nor does it mention litmus or classification.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions battery acid as an example of a strong acid but does not teach identifying common acids, bases, or salts using indicators. It only gives a safety warning about strong acids.

copy.en: Strong acids like battery acid are super dangerous because they can easily burn and damage many things!
copy.tl: Ang mga malalakas na asido tulad ng battery acid ay delikado dahil nakakapaso at nakakasira ng mga bagay!
copy.bis: Ang mga kusog nga asido sama sa battery acid delikado kaayo kay makapaso ug makadaot sa mga butang!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided investigations to infer the relationship among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits with varying number of loads and battery
assignedReviews.reason: The card only clarifies the terminology of a single cell versus a battery of multiple cells. It does not address current, voltage, resistance, series/parallel circuits, or any guided investigation, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Is a single AA battery really a 'battery'?

Scientifically, no! A single unit is a 'cell' (like one AA at 1.5 volts). A 'battery' is two or more cells connected — but everyday, we use both words!
copy.tl:
Talaga bang 'battery' ang isang AA?

Sa siyensya, hindi! Ang isang yunit ay 'cell' (tulad ng isang AA na 1.5 volts). Ang 'battery' ay dalawa o higit pang cells — pero sa araw-araw, pareho ang gamit!
copy.bis:
Tinuod ba nga 'battery' ang usa ka AA?

Sa siyensya, dili! Ang usa ka yunit mao ang 'cell' (sama sa usa ka AA nga 1.5 volts). Ang 'battery' duha o daghan nga cells — apan sa adlaw-adlaw, pareho ra!

assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions a battery's energy conversion; it does not involve assembling or drawing a simple circuit with wires, switch, bulb, motor, or buzzer, and no circuit representation is present.

copy.en: When a battery is used, its stored chemical energy magically changes into electrical energy, giving us the electricity we need!
copy.tl: Kapag ginagamit ang isang baterya, ang kemikal na enerhiya nito ay nagiging elektrikal na enerhiya, o kuryente!
copy.bis: Kung gamiton ang baterya, ang kemikal nga enerhiya niini mahimong elektrikal nga enerhiya, o kuryente!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: assemble and draw a simple circuit using batteries, wires, switch, and bulb and/or toy motor or buzzer
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the internal parts of a dry cell battery. assignedReviews.card_evidence: A carbon rod in the center (positive terminal), a zinc outer casing (negative terminal), and a paste electrolyte between them
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes battery construction but does not identify electricity as a flow of electrons or discuss safe handling of electricity. It is only tangentially related to electric current and electrical safety.

copy.en:
What's inside a dry cell battery?

A carbon rod in the center (positive terminal), a zinc outer casing (negative terminal), and a paste electrolyte between them that allows the chemical reaction!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nasa loob ng dry cell battery?

Isang carbon na baras sa gitna (positibong terminal), zinc na panlabas na balot (negatibong terminal), at isang pasta na electrolyte sa pagitan na nagpapahintulot ng chemical reaction!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang sulod sa dry cell battery?

Usa ka carbon nga baras sa tunga (positibong terminal), zinc nga gawas nga balat (negatibong terminal), ug pasta nga electrolyte sa taliwala nga nagtugot sa chemical reaction!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It just changes the chemical energy stored inside it into electrical energy.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe conservation of energy in everyday situations involving gravity, such as when objects fall
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes energy conversion in a battery, not conservation of energy in everyday situations involving gravity. It shares the broad topic of energy but does not directly support the competency's specific skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It just changes the chemical energy stored inside it into electrical energy.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses energy conversion, not the idea that energy can cause change including light, sound, and heat. It is related to energy but does not directly teach the competency's concept.

copy.en:
Does a battery create new energy?

Nope! It just changes the chemical energy stored inside it into electrical energy.
copy.tl:
Lumilikha ba ng bagong enerhiya ang baterya?

Hindi! Binabago lang nito ang nakaimbak na chemical energy sa loob nito para maging electrical energy.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes bees storing honey to survive when flowers are scarce, which is a behavioral adaptation, but it does not describe how animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage. It does not directly support the competency's focus on evolutionary change.

copy.en: Bees keep honey stored in their honeycomb — like a pantry, so they still have food to eat when flowers become scarce.
copy.tl: Iniimbak ng mga bubuyog ang pulot sa honeycomb — parang paminggalan, para may makain sila kapag kaunti na ang bulaklak.
copy.bis: Gitipigan sa mga putyukan ang dugos sa honeycomb — sama sa tipiganan, aron adunay makaon sila kon gamay na ang bulak.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A bee's body is built in three parts, with six legs and four wings
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes bee body parts (three parts, six legs, four wings) but does not identify their roles in movement or gathering food, which is the core action of G3-L-4. It only states the parts without explaining how they help the bee move or feed.

copy.en: A bee's body is built in three parts, with six legs and four wings — a perfectly designed little flying machine.
copy.tl: Ang katawan ng bubuyog ay may tatlong bahagi, anim na paa, at apat na pakpak — tunay na disenyo ng isang lumilipad na insekto.
copy.bis: Ang lawas sa putyukan adunay tulo ka bahin, unom ka tiil, ug upat ka pako — usa ka disenyo sa naglupad nga insekto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Beeswax! This natural wax from honeybees burns much cleaner than petroleum-derived paraffin candles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes in properties of materials when exposed to certain changes in temperature, such as changes when wood or coal are burned
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions burning but does not describe changes in material properties when exposed to temperature changes, nor does it discuss wood or coal burning. It only compares which candle burns cleaner.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: producing way less smoke and soot for you to breathe
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that changes in materials can be harmful to living and non-living things in the environment, such as trash disposal, and burning household materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions smoke and soot but does not explain how changes in materials can be harmful to living and non-living things, nor does it address trash disposal or burning household materials as environmental harm.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: burns much cleaner than petroleum-derived paraffin candles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how important types of chemical reactions, such as combustion, acids on metals, acids on carbonates, photosynthesis, and respiration, relate to or impact the natural and built environments using information from secondary sources
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on combustion indirectly but does not explain how combustion or other chemical reactions impact natural and built environments, nor does it use secondary sources.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This natural wax from honeybees burns much cleaner than petroleum-derived paraffin candles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that materials can burn but does not describe chemical properties such as reactivity, degradability, or biodegradability. It only states a comparative burning outcome.

copy.en:
Which candle burns cleaner: paraffin or beeswax?

Beeswax! This natural wax from honeybees burns much cleaner than petroleum-derived paraffin candles, producing way less smoke and soot for you to breathe.
copy.tl:
Aling kandila ang mas malinis ang pagkasunog: paraffin o beeswax?

Beeswax! Ang natural na wax na ito mula sa honeybees ay mas malinis masunog kaysa paraffin candles, na gumagawa ng mas kaunting usok at soot.
copy.bis:
Unsa nga kandila ang mas limpyo mosunog: paraffin o beeswax?

Beeswax! Kining natural nga wax gikan sa mga honeybee mas limpyo mosunog kaysa paraffin candles, nga nagprodyus og mas gamay nga aso ug soot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Beetles have hard wing covers called elytra that protect the soft flying wings folded underneath.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (elytra) and its protective role, but the competency requires identifying the role of outer body parts to move and to gather food. Protection is not movement or food gathering, so the card does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en: Beetles have hard wing covers called elytra that protect the soft flying wings folded underneath.
copy.tl: Ang mga salagubang ay may matigas na takip sa likod na tinatawag na elytra, na nagpoprotekta sa malalambot na pakpak na panlipad nila.
copy.bis: Ang mga bakukang adunay gahi nga takip sa likod nga gitawag og elytra, nga nagpanalipod sa humok nga pako nga gipilo sa ilalom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: People board up windows and bring pets inside to stay safe.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes human preparedness actions before a storm, not the typical weather conditions (e.g., cloud cover, wind, rain) before, during, or after a tropical cyclone. It shares the topic of tropical cyclones but does not directly support describing weather conditions.

copy.en:
What do people do before the storm peaks?

In the before stage, weather is turning! People board up windows and bring pets inside to stay safe.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ginagawa ng mga tao bago tumindi ang bagyo?

Sa before stage, nagbabago na ang panahon! Nagtatakip ang mga tao ng bintana at dinadala ang mga hayop sa loob.
copy.bis:
Unsay gibuhat sa mga tawo sa wala pa mosugod ang kusog nga bagyo?

Sa before stage, nag-usab na ang panahon! Gitakpan sa mga tawo ang mga bintana ug gidala ang mga hayop sa sulod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: check a PHIVOLCS map! Know if your house sits inside a permanent danger zone or a lahar path.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions PHIVOLCS and pre-eruption safety, but it focuses on hazard maps and danger zones, not on interpreting PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring Alert Levels or demonstrating actions before, during, and after an eruption. It does not directly support the competency's core skill.

copy.en: Before any eruption, families should check a PHIVOLCS map! Know if your house sits inside a permanent danger zone or a lahar path.
copy.tl: Bago sumabog, dapat alam ng pamilya kung ang bahay ay nasa permanenteng panganib na zona o nasa landas ng lahar ayon sa mapa ng PHIVOLCS.
copy.bis: Sa wala pa ang pagsabog, kinahanglan mahibalo ang pamilya kung ang balay anaa sa permanente nga delikadong zona o sa agianan sa lahar sumala sa mapa sa PHIVOLCS.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: pick a family meeting place outside the danger zone
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a general evacuation safety tip (choosing a meeting place) but does not interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring Alert Levels, which is the core action of the competency. It does not directly support demonstrating what to do before/during/after an eruption based on alert levels.

copy.en: Before unrest grows, pick a family meeting place outside the danger zone! This way, during an evacuation, no one waits on a close slope for others.
copy.tl: Bago lumala ang unrest, pumili ng family meeting place sa labas ng danger zone! Kaya during an evacuation, walang maghihintay sa malapit na slope para sa iba.
copy.bis: Sa wala pa mograbe ang unrest, pagpili og family meeting place sa gawas sa danger zone! Mao nga during an evacuation, walay maghulat sa duol nga slope para sa uban.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pack water, food, medicine, and a mask!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a generic emergency preparedness tip (pack a go-bag) but does not interpret PHIVOLCS alert levels or demonstrate specific before/during/after actions tied to volcanic eruption alert levels. It only mentions 'before alerts rise' without explaining alert levels or volcano-specific response.

copy.en:
What should you pack in your go-bag before alerts rise?

Pack water, food, medicine, and a mask! Leaving is much faster when your go-bag is already waiting by the door.
copy.tl:
Ano ang dapat ilagay sa go-bag bago umakyat ang babala?

Ilagay ang tubig, pagkain, gamot, at maskara! Mas mabilis umalis kung ang go-bag ay nasa pintuan na.
copy.bis:
Unsay ibutang sa go-bag sa wala pa ang alert?

Ibutang ang tubig, pagkaon, tambal, ug maskara! Mas paspas mo-gawas kung naa na daan sa pultahan ang bag.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: So they are ready! During a real alert, everyone already knows the exact meeting place and the safest route to take.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why communities practice eruption drills (preparedness, knowing meeting place and safe route) but does not teach PHIVOLCS alert levels or demonstrate specific before/during/after actions. It shares the topic of volcanic eruption safety but provides no direct instructional support for interpreting alert levels.

copy.en:
Why do communities near Mayon or Taal practice eruption drills?

So they are ready! During a real alert, everyone already knows the exact meeting place and the safest route to take.
copy.tl:
Bakit nag-eensayo ng eruption drills ang mga komunidad malapit sa Mayon o Taal?

Para handa sila! Kapag may totoong alert, alam na ng lahat ang meeting place at ang pinakaligtas na route.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga nag-praktis og eruption drills ang mga komunidad duol sa Mayon o Taal?

Aron andam sila! Kung tinuod nga alert, nahibalo na ang tanan sa meeting place ug pinakaluwas nga route.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: With the water cycle, there is increased crop yield, increased water storage, healthy animal and plant growth, and less sickness in people.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes benefits of the water cycle (crop yield, water storage, growth, health). It does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor their raw materials and products. No direct or prerequisite support for G8-L-9.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: healthy animal and plant growth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions healthy growth of animals and plants, which relates to basic needs like water, but it does not identify the basic needs (air, food, water, shelter) themselves. It only implies water's role through the water cycle, so it is related but not directly teaching the competency.

copy.en: With the water cycle, there is increased crop yield, increased water storage, healthy animal and plant growth, and less sickness in people.
copy.tl: Sa tulong ng water cycle, may tumataas na ani ng pananim, mas maraming water storage, malusog na paglaki ng mga hayop at halaman, at mas kaunting sakit sa mga tao.
copy.bis: Sa tabang sa water cycle, adunay mosaka nga ani sa tanom, mas daghan nga water storage, himsog nga pagtubo sa mga mananap ug tanom, ug mas gamay nga sakit sa mga tao.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: all thanks to subduction-related magmatism!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the subduction of an oceanic plate impacts on the plate above it
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions subduction-related magmatism as the cause of porphyry deposits, but it does not explain how subduction of an oceanic plate impacts the plate above it. It only states a connection without describing the mechanism or effects on the overriding plate.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most of the Philippines' gold and copper deposits, like those in Benguet, are porphyry deposits.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the location and distribution of active volcanoes, earthquake epicenters, and major mountain belts to the distribution of oceanic crust and continental crust
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses mineral deposits in the Philippines but does not relate the location/distribution of volcanoes, earthquake epicenters, or mountain belts to oceanic/continental crust distribution. The mention of subduction is not tied to these specific crustal features.

copy.en: Most of the Philippines' gold and copper deposits, like those in Benguet, are porphyry deposits. They form when magmatic fluids carrying metals fill cracks in rocks — all thanks to subduction-related magmatism!
copy.tl: Karamihan sa gold at copper deposits ng Pilipinas, tulad ng sa Benguet, ay porphyry deposits. Nabubuo sila kapag ang magmatic fluids na may metal ay pumupuno sa mga bitak ng bato — dahil sa subduction-related magmatism!
copy.bis: Kadaghanan sa gold ug copper deposits sa Pilipinas, sama sa sa Benguet, mga porphyry deposits. Naporma sila kung ang magmatic fluids nga nagdala og metal mopuno sa mga bitak sa bato — tungod sa subduction-related magmatism!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They have mined gold in Benguet for a long time
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the properties and uses of metals used by the local community such as iron, gold, silver, and copper
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions that gold was mined in Benguet long ago; it does not identify the properties or uses of gold or other metals as required by G3-M-9.

copy.en:
Who mined gold in Benguet long ago?

People in northern Luzon! They have mined gold in Benguet for a long time, even before the Spanish arrived.
copy.tl:
Sino ang nagmina ng ginto sa Benguet noong unang panahon?

Ang mga tao sa hilagang Luzon! Matagal na silang nagmimina ng ginto sa Benguet, kahit bago pa dumating ang mga Espanyol.
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang nagmina og bulawan sa Benguet kaniadto?

Ang mga tawo sa amihanang Luzon! Dugay na silang nagmina og bulawan sa Benguet, bisan sa wala pa moabot ang mga Katsila.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Betelgeuse is a bright reddish star shining in the constellation Orion!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the color and constellation of Betelgeuse. It does not address why ancient cultures relied on constellations for directions or seasons, which is the core of G6-E-9.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Betelgeuse is a bright reddish star shining in the constellation Orion!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a star (Betelgeuse) and its constellation, which is a natural object in the sky. However, it does not involve guided observation or description of multiple celestial objects, nor does it support the participatory activity described in G3-E-6.

copy.en:
What color is the star Betelgeuse in Orion?

Betelgeuse is a bright reddish star shining in the constellation Orion!
copy.tl:
Anong kulay ang bituing Betelgeuse sa Orion?

Ang Betelgeuse ay isang mapula-pula (red) na bituin sa konstelasyong Orion!
copy.bis:
Unsay kolor sa bituon nga Betelgeuse sa Orion?

Ang Betelgeuse usa ka mapula (red) nga bituon sa Orion!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is the second brightest star in Orion
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a fact about a star's brightness in a constellation. It does not explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations for directions or seasons, which is the core of G6-E-9.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Which star shines the second brightest in the Orion constellation?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a star (Betelgeuse) in the night sky, which is a natural object. However, it does not involve guided observation or description of multiple celestial objects as the competency requires; it is a single factual trivia item rather than an activity supporting observation and description.

copy.en:
Which star shines the second brightest in the Orion constellation?

That would be Betelgeuse! It is the second brightest star in Orion, shining right after the super bright Rigel.
copy.tl:
Aling bituin ang pangalawang pinakamaliwanag sa Orion?

Si Betelgeuse! Siya ang pangalawang pinakamaliwanag na bituin sa Orion, sumisilaw kasunod ng napakaliwanag na Rigel.
copy.bis:
Asang bituon ang ikaduhang pinakahayag sa Orion?

Si Betelgeuse! Siya ang ikaduhang pinakahayag nga bituon sa Orion, nagsilaw sunod sa hayag kaayo nga Rigel.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A huge red supergiant star located in the constellation Orion!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies Betelgeuse as a red supergiant star in Orion, which is a fact about a celestial object. However, G3-E-6 requires participation in guided activities to observe and describe natural objects in the sky, including stars. The card does not support the observational or descriptive activity; it merely states a classification. It shares vocabulary (star, constellation) but does not directly teach the skill of observing/describing sky objects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A huge red supergiant star located in the constellation Orion!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons
assignedReviews.reason: G6-E-9 asks students to explain why ancient cultures relied on constellations for directions and seasons. The card only identifies Betelgeuse as a star in Orion; it does not discuss constellations' use for navigation or seasonal verification. The mention of Orion is incidental and does not support the competency's explanatory goal.

copy.en:
What kind of star is Betelgeuse in the constellation Orion?

A huge red supergiant star located in the constellation Orion!
copy.tl:
Anong uri ng bituin ang Betelgeuse sa konstelasyong Orion?

Isang pulang higanteng bituin (red supergiant) na matatagpuan sa konstelasyong Orion!
copy.bis:
Unhong klase nga bituon ang Betelgeuse sa konstelasyon nga Orion?

Usa ka pula nga higante nga bituon (red supergiant) sa konstelasyon nga Orion!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the giant star Betelgeuse is expected to explode in a huge, bright blast called a supernova
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a star, which is a natural object in the sky, but it focuses on a future supernova event rather than guided observation and description of celestial objects as required by the competency. The content is not directly instructional for the G3-E-6 skill.

copy.en: Someday in the future, the giant star Betelgeuse is expected to explode in a huge, bright blast called a supernova!
copy.tl: Balang araw sa hinaharap, inaasahang sasabog ang malaking bituing Betelgeuse sa isang napakaliwanag na pagputok na tinatawag na supernova!
copy.bis: Sa umaabot, gilauman nga mobuto ang dako nga bituon nga Betelgeuse sa usa ka dako ug hayag nga pagbuto nga gitawag og supernova!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why is it easier to balance a bicycle when it's moving?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify inertia as the tendency for an object to stay at rest or in motion unless acted on by an unbalanced net force
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses balance and steering corrections while moving, not inertia as the tendency to stay at rest or in motion unless acted on by an unbalanced net force. It shares the topic of motion but does not directly teach the inertia concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When rolling, small steering movements can bring the bike back into balance
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe everyday situations that demonstrate: a. balanced forces such as a box resting on an inclined plane, a man standing still, or an object moving with constant velocity; b. unbalanced forces, such as freely falling fruit or an accelerating car
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a situation involving motion and balance, but it does not identify or describe balanced or unbalanced forces in the sense of the competency (e.g., box on inclined plane, constant velocity, accelerating car). The steering corrections are not framed as force balance examples.

copy.en:
Why is it easier to balance a bicycle when it's moving?

When rolling, small steering movements can bring the bike back into balance — but when still, there's nothing to correct the wobble!
copy.tl:
Bakit mas madaling balansehin ang bisikleta kapag gumagalaw?

Kapag gumagalaw, ang maliliit na paggalaw ng manibela ay nakakatulong na ibalik ito sa balanse — pero kapag nakatigil, walang maayos sa pag-alon!
copy.bis:
Ngano mas sayon nga balansehon ang bisikleta kon naglihok?

Kon naglihok, ang gagmay nga paglihok sa manibela makatabang nga mabalik kini sa balanse — apan kon naghunong, walay matambag sa paglingi!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its turning wheels reduce friction!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how friction can produce heat and investigate ways of reducing and increasing friction
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that wheels reduce friction, which is a way of reducing friction, but it does not demonstrate how friction produces heat nor investigate ways of reducing/increasing friction as the competency requires. It only mentions a single example without investigation or heat production.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why is it easier to roll a load on a bicycle with a sidecar?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe examples and uses of simple machines found at home, at school, and in the community
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses a bicycle with a sidecar as an example, which is a simple machine (wheel and axle), but it does not observe or describe examples and uses of simple machines found at home, school, or community. It only explains why wheels reduce friction, not the broader uses of simple machines.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its turning wheels reduce friction!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan and carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions friction reduction but does not plan or carry out a scientific investigation to determine the effect of different surfaces on the size of frictional forces. It provides no investigation, surfaces, or measurement, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
Why is it easier to roll a load on a bicycle with a sidecar?

Its turning wheels reduce friction! This makes it far easier to roll a heavy load than to just drag it.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas madaling itulak ang bigat sa bisikletang may sidecar?

Ang mga umiikot na gulong ay nagpapaliit ng friction! Kaya mas madaling itulak ang bigat kaysa kaladkarin ito.
copy.bis:
Nganong mas sayon iligid ang gibug-aton sa bisikleta nga adunay sidecar?

Ang nagtuyok nga mga ligid mokunhod sa friction! Busa mas sayon iligid ang gibug-aton kay sa pagguyod niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the bicycle was invented in 1817
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the invention of the bicycle and car with dates, but does not identify any scientist or their invention. It only mentions the inventions themselves, not the inventors, so it does not directly support the competency of identifying a famous scientist and their invention.

copy.en: Believe it or not, the bicycle was invented in 1817, which came long before the first gasoline car in 1886!
copy.tl: Hindi mo maniwala, pero nauna ang bisikleta noong 1817 bago pa man ang unang kotseng de-gasolina noong 1886!
copy.bis: Dili gyud nimo tinuohan, pero una ang bisikleta niadtong 1817 sa dili pa ang unang awto nga gasolina niadtong 1886!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The very first bicycle, known as the draisine, was invented way back in the year 1817!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an invention (the draisine) but does not identify any scientist or inventor by name, nor does it involve using secondary sources. It only states the year of invention, so it does not directly support the competency's requirement to identify a famous scientist and their invention.

copy.en:
What year was the first bicycle, the draisine, invented?

The very first bicycle, known as the draisine, was invented way back in the year 1817!
copy.tl:
Anong taon nang-imbento ang unang bisikleta, ang draisine?

Ang unang bisikleta, na kilala bilang draisine, ay inimbento noong taong 1817!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga tuig ang na-imbento ang unang bisikleta, ang draisine?

Ang unang bisikleta, nga nailhan nga draisine, na-imbento niadtong tuig 1817!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: there was no sound because space has no air to carry it
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that sound cannot travel in space because there is no air, which touches on the idea that sound needs a medium. However, the competency focuses on exploring and describing how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations (e.g., ringing a bell, hearing noises). The card is about the Big Bang, not an everyday situation, and does not describe how sound is made or transferred; it only notes the absence of sound in a vacuum. This is related background knowledge about sound transmission but does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en: Even though it is called the Big Bang, there was no sound because space has no air to carry it!
copy.tl: Kahit tinawag itong Big Bang, walang tunog na narinig dahil walang hangin sa espasyo na magdadala ng tunog!
copy.bis: Bisan gitawag kini nga Big Bang, walay tingog nga nadungog kay ang espasyo walay hangin nga magdala sa tingog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can easily find Polaris, the North Star, just by using the two outer stars of the Big Dipper!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations to indicate directions and verify seasons
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a method for locating Polaris using the Big Dipper. It does not explain why ancient human cultures relied on constellations for direction-finding or season verification, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can easily find Polaris, the North Star, just by using the two outer stars of the Big Dipper!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions stars and a constellation, but it does not guide observation or description of natural objects seen in the sky, nor does it cover the Sun, Moon, planets, or stars generally. It is only topically related to celestial objects.

copy.en: You can easily find Polaris, the North Star, just by using the two outer stars of the Big Dipper!
copy.tl: Madali mong matutunton ang Polaris o North Star gamit lang ang dalawang panlabas na bituin ng Big Dipper!
copy.bis: Sayon ra nimo makit-an ang Polaris o North Star pinaagi sa duha ka gawas nga bituon sa Big Dipper!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: weigh up to about 11 kilograms
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)

Giunsa nasayod sa langgam ang direksyon?

Daghang migratory nga langgam adunay sulod nga pagbati sa magnetic field sa Yuta — morag adunay built-in nga kompas nga motabang nila sa taas nga paglupad.

How do night-flying birds find their way?

Some birds that migrate at night follow the patterns of the stars, almost like reading the sky as a map!

Paano nahahanap ng ibon ang daan sa gabi?

May mga ibong lumilipat sa gabi na sumusunod sa padron ng mga bituin, parang binabasa nilang mapa ang kalangitan!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpangita sa dalan sa langgam sa gabii?

Adunay mga langgam nga mobalhin sa gabii nga mosunod sa han-ay sa mga bitoon, morag gibasa nila ang langit ingong mapa!

Maraming ibon ang gumagamit ng posisyon ng araw at mga bituin para malaman ang tamang direksyon sa kanilang paglipat.

Unsaon nahibalo sa langgam ang direksyon?

Daghang langgam ang mogamit sa posisyon sa adlaw ug sa mga bitoon aron mahibaloan ang husto nga direksyon sa ilang pagbalhin.

copy.tl: Ang ibong nakatungtong sa isang power line ay hindi nakukuryente dahil pareho ang boltahe sa dalawang paa nito, kaya walang current na dumadaloy sa katawan nito!
copy.bis: Ang langgam nga naglingkod sa usa ka power line dili makuryente tungod kay parehas ra ang boltahe sa duha niini ka tiil, mao nga walay current nga moagi sa lawas niini!

Why don't bird feathers get soaked in water?

Many birds take oil from a gland near their tail and spread it over their feathers with their beak — this keeps feathers strong and water-resistant.
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi basang-basa ang balahibo ng ibon?

Sinasagap ng maraming ibon ang langis mula sa glandula malapit sa buntot at ipinapahid ito sa balahibo gamit ang tuka — kaya matibay at hindi nababasa ang balahibo.
copy.bis:
Ngano dili kaayo mabasa ang balhibo sa langgam?

Daghang langgam mokuha og lana gikan sa glandula duol sa ikog ug ipahid kini sa ilang balhibo gamit ang sungo — mao nga molig-on ug dili kaayo mabasa ang balhibo.

By the stars! Some night-flying birds learn to read the center of the sky's rotation near north to know which way to go.

Paano nakakahanap ng direksyon ang ibong lumilipad sa gabi?

Sa mga bituin! Natutunan ng ilang ibong lumilipad sa gabi na basahin ang sentro ng pag-ikot ng kalangitan malapit sa hilaga para malaman ang direksyon.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagpangita og direksyon sa langgam nga molupad sa gabii?

Pinaagi sa mga bituon! Makakat-on ang pipila ka langgam nga molupad sa gabii pagbasa sa sentro sa pagtuyok sa kalangitan duol sa amihanan aron mahibal-an ang direksyon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: hollow bones, a light beak, and feathers — all so it can fly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions outer parts (beak, feathers) but frames them as adaptations for flight, not as body parts whose role is to move or gather food. It also includes internal features (hollow bones) and does not address gathering food. This does not directly teach the competency's skill of identifying outer body parts and their roles in movement and food gathering.

copy.en: A bird's whole body is built strong yet light — hollow bones, a light beak, and feathers — all so it can fly.
copy.tl: Ang katawan ng ibon ay matibay pero magaan — may guwang na buto, magaang tuka, at balahibo — lahat para makalipad ito.
copy.bis: Ang tibuok lawas sa langgam lig-on apan gaan — adunay guwang nga bukog, gaan nga sungo, ug balhibo — tanan aron makalupad kini.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the sun's apparent motion, but it does not support the competency's focus on guided activities to explore and record how and when celestial objects move. It is a fact about bird navigation, not an instructional activity about celestial motion.

copy.en: Some birds use the sun's position as a compass! Since the sun moves across the sky during the day, they combine it with an internal clock to keep their direction correct.
copy.tl: Ginagamit ng ilang ibon ang posisyon ng araw bilang kompas! Dahil gumagalaw ang araw sa buong araw, isinasabay nila ito sa kanilang panloob na orasan para manatiling tama ang direksyon.
copy.bis: Ang pipila ka langgam mogamit sa posisyon sa adlaw isip kompas! Tungod kay molihok ang adlaw sa langit sa tibuok adlaw, gisagol nila kini sa ilang sulod nga orasan aron magpabilin nga husto ang direksyon.

copy.en:
Can birds remember where they hid food?

Some birds can remember where they hid thousands of seeds, so they can go back for them when they're hungry!
copy.tl:
Nakakatanda ba ang ibon kung saan sila nagtago ng pagkain?

May mga ibong nakakaalala kung saan nila itinago ang libu-libong buto, para mabalikan ito kapag gutom na sila!
copy.bis:
Makahinumdom ba ang langgam kon asa niya gitago ang pagkaon?

Naay mga langgam nga makahinumdom kon asa nila gitago ang linibo ka liso aron mabalikan kini kung gigutom na sila!

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the beak as an outer body part, but its role is thermoregulation (cooling), not moving or gathering food as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Birds have no sweat glands, so they open their beaks and breathe fast to let heat evaporate from inside their mouths.

copy.en:
Why do birds open their beaks when it's hot?

Birds have no sweat glands, so they open their beaks and breathe fast to let heat evaporate from inside their mouths.
copy.tl:
Bakit nagbubuka ng tuka ang ibon kapag mainit?

Wala kasing pawisan ang mga ibon, kaya ibinubuka nila ang tuka at mabilis huminga para singawan ang init sa loob ng bibig nila.
copy.bis:
Ngano moabli sa tuka ang langgam kon init?

Walay singot ang mga langgam, mao nga ablihan nila ang tuka ug paspas moginhawa aron mosingaw ang kainit sa sulod sa baba nila.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a beak and feathers, which are outer body parts, but it does not describe their role in moving or gathering food. Preening is a cleaning/maintenance behavior, not locomotion or feeding, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.reason: Preening is a behavioral maintenance activity, not an example of an animal having changed to better suit its environment through adaptation such as mimicry or camouflage. The card does not describe evolutionary change or environmental adaptation.

copy.en: A bird oils and smooths its feathers with its beak so they stay sleek and shed water — this cleaning ritual is called preening.
copy.tl: Nililinis at pinapahiran ng ibon ng langis ang kanyang mga balahibo gamit ang tuka para manatiling makinis at hindi basain ng tubig — tinatawag itong preening.
copy.bis: Limpyohan ug pahiran og lana sa langgam ang iyang mga balhibo gamit ang tuka aron magpabiling hapsay ug dili mabasa — gitawag kini og preening.

copy.tl: Pinagpapagaspas ng mga ibon ang kanilang mga pakpak upang itulak ang sarili paitaas at pasulong sa hangin!
copy.bis: Ginakapay-kapay sa mga langgam ang ilang mga pako aron itukmod ang ilang kaugalingon paitaas ug pasulong sa hangin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it doesn't push hard against the air

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a push against air but does not demonstrate how pushes or pulls change an object's speed or direction. It focuses on energy saving during bird flight, not on force effects on motion.

copy.en: On the upstroke, a bird partly folds its wing so it doesn't push hard against the air. This saves energy while bringing the wing back up to flap again!
copy.tl: Sa upstroke, bahagyang itinitiklop ng ibon ang pakpak para hindi masyadong humampas sa hangin. Ginagawa ito para mas kaunti ang lakas na nasasayang habang ibinabalik ang pakpak pataas!
copy.bis: Sa upstroke, gamayng gipilo sa langgam ang iyang pako aron dili kusog nga moigo sa hangin. Aron dyutay ra ang kusog nga mausik samtang gibalik ang pako pataas!

copy.en:
Are a newly hatched chick's bones already hollow?

Not yet! A newly hatched chick's bones aren't fully hollow. As it grows and learns to fly, the insides of some bones slowly become more hollow.
copy.tl:
Guwang na ba agad ang buto ng bagong-pisang sisiw?

Hindi pa! Hindi pa ganap na guwang ang buto ng sisiw kapag bagong pisa. Habang lumalaki at natututong lumipad, unti-unting gumuguwang ang loob ng ilang buto nito.
copy.bis:
Hawan na ba dayon ang buto sa bag-ong napusa nga piso?

Dili pa! Dili pa hingpit nga hawan ang buto sa piso kung bag-o pa mapusa. Samtang nagdako ug nagkat-on molupad, anam-anam nga mahawan ang sulod sa ubang buto niini.
